title: Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe Reservation Restoration Act
official_summary:
Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe Reservation Restoration Act

This bill directs the Department of Agriculture to transfer to the administrative jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to approximately 11,760 acres of identified federal land in the Chippewa National Forest in Cass County, Minnesota. Immediately upon transfer, the federal land shall be held in trust for the benefit of the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe and considered as a part of its reservation.

The federal land shall not become eligible or be used for gaming activities under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

summary.headline: A 2020 law moves about 11,760 acres of Chippewa National Forest land in Minnesota into trust for the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe and makes it part of their reservation.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Department of Agriculture to transfer about 11,760 acres of federal land in Cass County, Minnesota, from the Chippewa National Forest to the Department of the Interior. Once transferred, the land is held in trust for the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe and treated as part of its reservation. The land cannot be used for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

who_it_affects.group: Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe members
who_it_affects.how: The tribe gains trust ownership of about 11,760 acres that become part of its reservation.

who_it_affects.group: People who use the Chippewa National Forest for recreation or other activities
who_it_affects.how: The identified acres would move out of national forest management and into tribal trust land under the Department of the Interior.
The transferred land cannot be used for gaming activities under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law became effective on December 23, 2020, when it was enacted. The summary does not give a separate date for completing the land transfer.
